mainEntity.name: What exactly is still life photography?

acceptedAnswer.text: Still life photography is a specialised genre within fine art photography that concentrates on photographing inanimate subjects, which can be either natural or man-made. This form of photography aims to produce artistic images and has its roots in the early days of photography when capturing moving subjects was challenging.

mainEntity.name: What does still photography refer to?

acceptedAnswer.text: Still photography is a term used to describe a standard photograph that is not part of a video or film.

mainEntity.name: What are the two primary categories of still life photography?

acceptedAnswer.text: Still life photography can be divided into two main types: found and created. Found still life involves photographing a random assortment of objects as they are found, without rearranging them for the photo. Created still life, on the other hand, involves deliberately arranging objects to achieve a desired composition.

mainEntity.name: What qualifies as a still life photograph?

acceptedAnswer.text: A still life photograph typically features inanimate subjects, often everyday items that can be either natural (such as food, flowers, or dead animals) or human-made (like drinking glasses, books, or jewellery). These are depicted in a way that focuses on their aesthetic and compositional qualities.
